title: Fear not Ellettsville, this Trojan Horse actually comes in peace - NewsBreak
text:
By Stephen Herzog ,
9 hours ago
Based on Greek mythology, folks living in Ellettsville might be getting a little nervous.
After some uncertainty about the current state of affairs and future plans, the owners of the Trojan Horse restaurant explained why they're moving northwest .
But fear not, Ellettsville residents, you're not getting a restaurant secretly filled with warriors (no offense to the Trojan Horse staff). You're getting an eatery Bloomington folks came to love over the past couple decades.
Business news, especially involving restaurants, is often bittersweet. A favorite leaves, but maybe a new favorite replaces it. We fondly remember times at long gone local businesses, but sadly wish we could relive those experiences.
A little foreshadowing for regular readers, in Friday's It's Your Business column, Talisha Coppock of Downtown Bloomington Inc. discusses the ongoing state of affairs with business.
"Roughly 40 downtown Bloomington businesses are more than 40 years old, making them part of the city’s 'legacy business' class: places that are not just storefronts, but local landmarks," she writes. "Many were opened or long operated by Baby Boomer owners who are wanting a change of pace as they approach retirement age. That raises a difficult question for Bloomington: what happens when the people who built these businesses are ready to try something different, step away entirely or substantially change the culture of their business?"
The landscape is ever-changing. Remember to take advantage of opportunities while they're here, and stay open to the idea of what's next.
Speaking of "what's next," here's more of what's been happening this week in Bloomington.
While you're reading The Herald-Times this next week, know that we're doing our best to provide you with what we think is the most important news happening locally and in the surrounding region. If you see or know something we might want to pursue, just send an email to mediatips@heraldt.com
In case you missed it 🚧 Route recalculation: College Avenue, south of Third Street will be closing from June 30 through July 24 to allow construction crews to complete the enclosure of the skybridge between the old and new portions of the Bloomington Convention Center. The closure would include the western sidewalk and the existing eastern pedestrian diversion.
👩🏼‍⚖️ Continuing jail saga: While Monroe County may face a lawsuit from the ACLU over unconstitutional jail conditions, legal experts say any court action could be months away, but officials have an obligation to act now. The American Civil Liberties Union of Indiana alleged in a 2008 lawsuit that the Monroe County Jail’s overcrowding violated state and federal constitutions.
The county now plans to spend another $41 million to build a new 250-bed community corrections building, in part to address overcrowding at the new jail.
The big story this week 🎗️ Missing, but not forgotten: On the 15th anniversary of the disappearance of Indiana University student Lauren Spierer, authorities continue to ask the public for any information regarding the case, no matter how small it may seem.
Spierer, 20 at the time of her disappearance on June 3, 2011, was last seen at 4:30 a.m. at the intersection of 11th Street and College Avenue, walking home alone after a night out at Kilroy’s Sports Bar and downtown apartments. Despite numerous searches, including at a landfill, no clues about her disappearance have been found.
BPD said in a news release June 2 that in the last year, officers investigated 23 new tips that resulted in “multiple interviews.” Detectives share information “regularly” with local, state and federal law enforcement agencies.
This article originally appeared on The Herald-Times: Fear not Ellettsville, this Trojan Horse actually comes in peace
